transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-31 14:00 PDT — Duration ~45 minutes
Attendees: Samantha Lee, Evan Rhee, Maya Patel (Redwood); Robert Miller, Priya Singh, Liam O'Connor, Hannah Cho (Maple City Bank)

[00:00] Samantha Lee: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is our weekly POC security sync for Maple City bank, um quick round robin — we, we have Evan on for the se side and Maya from CS, and on your side?
[00:08] Robert Miller: hey all, Robert here, thanks Samantha. Priya, Liam, Hannah on our side.
[00:12] Priya Singh: hi, yeah thanks.
[00:15] Samantha Lee: great. quick agenda: sso/saml and scim, audit logs and retention, soc2 evidence questions, and any blockers for the pilot. sound ok?
[00:23] Robert Miller: yep, that works.
[00:27] Evan Rhee: quick note, we'll follow up with a small benchmark run next week once we have the okta test users — that'll be SE + your devops.
[00:34] Priya Singh: perfect. first question — can you confirm how SSO is integrated for the pilot? we're using Okta and need to know if you support SAML 2.0 + SCIM provisioning out of the box. also, role mapping and RBAC?
[00:45] Samantha Lee: yes, we support SAML 2.0; we have a default SAML flow and support SCIM provisioning. for RBAC you can map Okta groups to Redwood roles; our standard mapping docs are in the security pack. i'll attach again after the call.
[00:56] Priya Singh: and SCIM is optional, we prefer provisioning via SCIM to avoid manual user creation. does SCIM support passing department and manager attributes? we need those for separation of duties reviews.
[01:05] Evan Rhee: mm yes — SCIM extends attributes, we can accept custom attributes and map them to role claims. there might be a small mapping config on our end; i'll send sample mapping.
[01:14] Hannah Cho: are there any known issues with automatic deprovisioning? we need prompt revocation when users leave.
[01:20] Evan Rhee: deprovisioning is supported; token invalidation happens within a minute or two for sessions, and we can revoke session tokens immediately for admin-triggered events via API.
[01:30] Priya Singh: good. next — audit logs. we need to see a sample of what audit logs look like, the fields, and whether we can export them to our Splunk/ELK ingestion. also retention policy — we typically require 365 days for audit trails.
[01:45] Samantha Lee: we have structured audit logs with timestamp, user id, action, resource, request id, ip, and model/route metadata. we can stream logs to your S3 or push to a syslog endpoint; many customers pull via our secure export. i'll include sample JSON snippets in the pack. retention default in hosted is 90 days, but for dedicated/private we can configure longer retention. for the pilot we can provide a 365-day retention export snapshot — operationally that's an export rather than live retention for the hosted tier.
[02:12] Priya Singh: ok so for hosted api pilot it's an export snapshot — that won't satisfy our compliance team unless we can prove continuous retention. is dedicated the only way to get live 365 day retention?
[02:25] Samantha Lee: correct, dedicated or private deployment with customer-managed storage gives you live retention and the controls needed for audit. for hosted we can meet many needs via exports and immutable audit bundles for the pilot.
[02:36] Robert Miller: what's the difference from a compliance perspective between dedicated and private? we want to understand tradeoffs — cost vs control.
[02:44] Evan Rhee: dedicated gives you isolated capacity and configurable retention, but runs in Redwood's managed control plane. private/VPC gives you a customer control plane option and can be fully on-prem; that adds more control for encryption keys and network isolation but comes with more ops overhead.
[02:59] Priya Singh: speaking of keys — KMS/HSM integration. we need to use our KMS for customer-owned key management for data at rest. is that available?
[03:10] Samantha Lee: yes, for private and dedicated we support KMS integrations — either cloud KMS or an HSM-based flow. for hosted, we offer envelope encryption and can support customer-managed keys in some enterprise plans; i'll flag that and add detail in the pack.
[03:24] Priya Singh: and what about encryption of logs and audit trails? must be encrypted at rest with keys we control.
[03:30] Evan Rhee: logs exported to your S3 can be encrypted with your bucket keys; internal retention in dedicated can be set to use your KMS. we'll document exactly which fields are encrypted and the key ownership model.
[03:41] Liam O'Connor: on the data plane — during the pilot we'll be sending redacted PII, but i want to confirm default data retention and whether there's automatic PII scrubbing.
[03:52] Samantha Lee: by default we retain inputs for 90 days in hosted; we have a PII scrubbing capability that can mask or drop sensitive fields at ingestion via a pipeline rule. for the pilot we can enable stricter scrubbing and show logs of scrubbing operations.
[04:06] Priya Singh: can scrubbing be configured with custom regex and tokens? we have account numbers and other formats.
[04:12] Evan Rhee: yes, we support custom patterns and tokenization rules; we'll need sample patterns from you. Evan: i can run a small test that redacts a sample set and share the before/after.
[04:23] Samantha Lee: action item for Evan to run KV-cache scrub test and share results within 48 hours.
[04:28] Robert Miller: another item — SOC2. we need to see the SOC2 Type II report excerpt and understand which controls map to our requirements. also evidence for change management and access reviews.
[04:39] Samantha Lee: we are SOC2 Type II compliant; we'll send a redacted report and a controls-mapping document. note: the full report is under NDA normally, we'll provide an excerpt and a summary of control owners. next steps will include exchange of NDAs if needed for full report access.
[04:56] Priya Singh: ok, please include the controls mapping to detectability of config changes and access logs.
[05:02] Samantha Lee: absolutely.
[05:05] Hannah Cho: what about vulnerability scanning and pen test cadence? we need recent pentest results and remediation timelines.
[05:12] Evan Rhee: we run quarterly vulnerability scans and annual external pentests. we can share recent pen-test summary and status of high/critical remediations.
[05:21] Priya Singh: for the pilot we may want to run a small scoped pentest on the integration points — SCIM/SAML endpoints and our ingest path. is that supported?
[05:31] Samantha Lee: yes, we can coordinate a scoped test with our security team; usually we require a pre-scope form and allow testing windows. i'll include the process doc.
[05:40] Robert Miller: networking question — if we go with private or VPC, can we do IP allowlist plus private peering?
[05:48] Evan Rhee: yes, we support VPC peering, private links, and strict IP allowlists for dedicated/private deployments.
[05:55] Priya Singh: audit log ingestion — is there an API to pull logs or is it push only?
[06:01] Samantha Lee: both; you can pull via secure API and we also support push exports to S3 or SIEM connectors. logs are signed with a signature header for integrity verification.
[06:11] Liam O'Connor: great. about retention during the pilot — maple city's compliance will probably require archived audit trails for 365 days. is a one-off export acceptable as evidence?
[06:21] Samantha Lee: for pilots often we produce an immutable export package containing event streams for the pilot period; for continuous retention you'd want dedicated/private. we'll provide the export and also a mechanism to validate integrity (signed manifests).
[06:35] Priya Singh: ok that might work for now but we'll confirm with the compliance team.
[06:40] Samantha Lee: quick note on telemetry: our runtime collects per-token latency metrics plus route-level traces. we can share anonymized traces for the pilot to help with tuning without exposing customer content.
[06:52] Priya Singh: and is content ever used for model training?
[06:55] Samantha Lee: for hosted, by default we do not use customer content for training; enterprise agreements explicitly state training use is disabled. we'll include contract language.
[07:04] Robert Miller: good to have that in writing.
[07:06] Hannah Cho: about logs, can we get JSON schema for the audit events? that helps our parsers.
[07:12] Evan Rhee: yes, sample schema in the pack.
[07:15] Priya Singh: can you also include a sample of an auth log for a failed login, admin action and a model call with token? we need both user admin actions and data plane events.
[07:25] Samantha Lee: yes — will do.
[07:28] Robert Miller: on timelines — SOC2 review is on our critical path; we need to get evidence within the next two weeks to feed our risk assessment ahead of the pilot extension decision.
[07:39] Priya Singh: which specific artifacts are you sharing for SOC2? is it the entire report or a subset?
[07:43] Samantha Lee: redacted report, controls matrix, change management artifacts (ticketing snapshots), and audit log samples. full report requires NDA.
[07:53] Priya Singh: ok. next technical note — are there any known quirks with session tokens being cached at load balancer level? i recall a past issue with session stickiness.
[08:02] Evan Rhee: we changed our session handling last quarter; session invalidation is now immediate on revoke for new pods. older pods can have a slight TTL but we won't see multi-minute hangs anymore. we'll include specifics in release notes.
[08:14] Liam O'Connor: thanks. can we get an endpoint for programmatic session revocation?
[08:18] Samantha Lee: yes, admin API supports immediate revoke; i'll add API docs link.
[08:22] Priya Singh: about PII — i want to run a small test: we'll send a sample dataset with account numbers and names and want to validate that scrubbing rules are removing account numbers and only leaving tokens. can you confirm workflow?
[08:34] Evan Rhee: send sample patterns and sample data to our secure upload link; we'll run scrub and return before/after with hashes to prove redaction. we'll limit access to the scrubbed artifacts.
[08:46] Samantha Lee: action: Evan to run scrub test and share within 48 hours.
[08:50] Robert Miller: good. anything about incident response? we need SLAs for incident notification for pilot and a point of contact.
[08:59] Samantha Lee: our incident process: severity definitions, 1hr P1 notification, postmortem within 72h for P1; contact will be Maya for this POC — i'll share the oncall rota.
[09:10] Maya Patel: happy to be the contact.
[09:12] Priya Singh: ok great. last items — pricing impact of enabling 365 retention or dedicated: what's the ballpark?
[09:22] Samantha Lee: dedicated pricing is typically a monthly reserved capacity model; retention extension adds storage, pricing depends on capacity. we'll include a ballpark in the pricing doc; i'll ask pricing to give a pilot uplift estimate for a one-month dedicated slice.
[09:36] Robert Miller: can we get a short-lived dedicated environment for pilot?
[09:40] Samantha Lee: we can run a short 30-day dedicated pilot but need advanced notice; evan and i can scope minimal capacity.
[09:48] Priya Singh: ok, that's interesting — will discuss internally.
[09:52] Samantha Lee: recap of action items: 1) send security pack with SOC2 excerpt and audit log samples (Samantha) 2) Evan run KV-cache scrub and scrub test and share results (Evan) 3) Maple City to provide Okta SAML metadata and sample users (Liam) 4) Priya to confirm retention decision (Priya). we'll add due dates in the CRM.
[10:14] Robert Miller: sounds good. any blockers from Redwood side?
[10:18] Samantha Lee: none at the moment, just awaiting your Okta metadata and retention confirmation.
[10:22] Priya Singh: we'll try to get metadata by end of next week.
[10:26] Samantha Lee: perfect. i'll send the security pack by Friday (2026-04-02). thanks everyone.
[10:30] Robert Miller: thanks.
[10:32] Priya Singh: thanks, bye.
[10:34] Hannah Cho: thanks.

End of transcript.

References in call: security pack (Redwood_Security_Pack_v2.pdf), sample audit log JSON (audit_sample_2026-03.json), SOC2_excerpt_redacted.pdf, Okta metadata to be shared by Maple City, sample KV-cache scrub test link (redwood://poc/kv-scrub/results).

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker overlap and short crosstalk; proper nouns sometimes transcribed with spaces (e.g., K V cache).
